question: Which country was ranked highest for gender equality in the Global Gender Gap Report, 2025, released by the World Economic Forum in May 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iceland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iceland** ranked the highest in the **Global Gender Gap Report 2025**, continuing its legacy as the most gender-equal nation globally.
 
• Iceland has been consistently performing well in gender equality metrics such as **economic participation, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment**.
 
• The nation has achieved nearly **91.2%** of gender parity, according to the World Economic Forum's latest report.
 
• Iceland’s success is attributed to progressive policies like **mandatory parental leave for both genders, equal pay laws, and strong representation of women in politics and business**.
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Report**, published by the **World Economic Forum**, evaluates gender equality across nations using various indices and is considered a crucial tool for assessing global progress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Gender Gap Report:**

 
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Report** was first introduced by the **World Economic Forum** in **2006**.
 
• It measures gender equality across four dimensions: **Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment**.
 
• The report ranks countries based on their performance in closing the gender gap, with **0 representing absolute inequality** and **1 representing absolute equality**.
 
• It serves as a crucial benchmark for policymakers to address gender disparities globally.
 
 
 
• **Iceland’s Gender Equality Initiatives:**
 
 
• Iceland has a **mandatory parental leave policy**, where both parents are entitled to three months of leave, ensuring shared parenting responsibilities.
 
• The country passed **equal pay legislation in 2018**, requiring companies to prove they pay men and women equally.
 
• Women in Iceland hold significant political representation, with over **40% of parliamentary seats** occupied by women.
 
• Public protests, such as the **1975 Women’s Strike**, played a critical role in shaping Iceland’s gender equality policies.
 
 
 
• **Other High-Ranking Countries:**
 
 
• **Norway:** Known for its robust policies on gender equality, including strong parental leave and workplace equality programs.
 
• **Sweden:** A pioneer in gender-neutral policies and equal representation in government and corporate sectors.
 
• **Germany:** Despite significant advancements, Germany trails behind Nordic countries in achieving full gender parity.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Gender Equality:**
 
 
• Gender equality is essential for achieving **sustainable development** and ensuring social justice.
 
• It contributes to higher economic productivity and fosters a more inclusive society.
 
• Eliminating gender disparities is crucial for achieving global goals like the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5**, which focuses on gender equality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Trends:** Iceland has been ranked **first** in the Global Gender Gap Report for more than a decade, showcasing its consistent commitment to gender equality.
 
• **Impact of Policies:** Iceland’s proactive measures, such as equal pay laws and gender quotas, have significantly influenced its performance.
 
• **Global Challenges:** Despite progress in some countries, global gender parity is projected to take over **130 years** to achieve, highlighting the need for accelerated efforts.
